messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED #eng-oncall — p99 latency spike detected for service=contbatch-usw2 at 2025-04-12T15:02:47Z. p99 = 3.8s, p95 = 1.2s. Auto-page to oncall.
sara: saw it, joining. can someone pull the p99 heatmap?
mike: grabbing metrics now. initial look: tail spike aligns with continuous-batching scheduler backlog + a short stream-stall window.
anya: likely mixed-seqlen amplification — a few very long seqs are blocking packers, causing huge pack sizes then long KV paging.
sara: impact? any customer-facing errors?
leo: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/in/dash/contbatch?from=now-30m&to=now — traffic up ~12% last 10m, error rate steady. percent of requests >2s jumped from 0.6% -> 5.1% in last 5m.
ops-bot: deploys: none in last 30m. Autoscaler triggered one ramp 6m ago.
mike: digging traces — streaming RPCs show stalls where streamer blocks on batch assembly for ~2.4s then long kernel time. KV eviction churn also spikes.
anya: config snapshot: contbatch scheduler config (usw2):
```
pack_max_tokens: 2048
pack_timeout_ms: 12
fair_share_alpha: 0.2
mixed_seq_threshold: 512
```
sara: can we quick reduce pack_max_tokens or reduce timeout to break huge packs?
mike: I can lower pack_max_tokens to 1024 and pack_timeout_ms to 6ms. will push to canary on one pod group in us-west-2.
leo: starting the canary now — group: contbatch-usw2-zone-c.
ops-bot: canary rollout started for contbatch-usw2-zone-c (rev=2025.04.12-ctb-rc3).
sara: monitoring p95/p99 on the canary. mike — paste the rollback command if we need it.
mike: rollback cmd: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/contbatch-zone-c -n prod`
anya: also enabling prefix-KV caching for the heavy request path temporarily (`kv.prefix_cache=true`) — should reduce eviction.
leo: canary metrics 45s in: p99 down from 3.8s -> 1.5s on canary, p95 stable at ~0.9s. overall cluster p99 still 3.6s.
sara: good. continue canary. set alert to suppress pages to avoid noise. I'll annotate incident.
ops-bot: Pager suppression set for contbatch p99 alert for 10m by sara.
mike: note — we still see streaming stalls tied to long seqs. long-term we should add seq-length-based scheduling priority and preemptive pack splitting. filing a ticket.
anya: filed INF-7892: "seqlen-aware preemptive packer + pack-split heuristic" with priority P1.
simon: i'm taking handoff in 10m (15:15Z). leaving runbook steps in thread.
sara: handoff accepted. next steps for simon: 1) finish canary to 50% across zones, 2) monitor kv eviction rate and successful prefix cache hits, 3) if p99 <=1.6s for 5m proceed to full rollout, else rollback.
simon: noted. will also coordinate with customer-sre if we need to notify any impacted customers (only small % impacted so far).
leo: customer impact note: 4 customer traffic clusters had >2s responses for ~3-6min windows. none exceeded SLA window (30m) but we should prep comms if patterns persist.
sara: tagging product & cs for visibility: @leo @mike — please add a short impact summary in the incident tracker.
mike: adding summary to INC-20250412-ctb-tail.
anya: follow-up action items: A) pack_max tuning + pack_timeout rollback guard, B) seqlen-aware packer ticket (INF-7892), C) KV cache instrumentation improvements (INF-7893).
simon: I'm on-call from 15:15Z->23:15Z. will monitor and continue rollout if canary looks good. dropping a marker in ops log.
ops-bot: Handoff: sara -> simon at 15:15Z recorded.
sara: thanks team. I will close the initial page when full rollout completes or we rollback. keep updates short here. :thumbsup:
